Complete read: Fuses the initial leading linear combination, alternates one full-size scratch vector with output, and chooses parity so the final value lands in output without an extra copy. Zero/constant/linear and whole-owner alias paths are explicit. Hyper's affine conversion already updates an owned vector in reverse order; no generic composition port selected.

Complete read: Builds paired coefficient blocks, repeatedly squares the inner polynomial, and merges blocks bottom-up in preplanned scalar storage plus two power buffers. Skips only coefficients proved zero. All initialized workspace slots are cleared; geometric sizes assume valid bounded input lengths. Native archived execution is not claimed.

Complete archived-only read: Computes the constant atan separately and integrates f'/(1+f^2), capturing source-dependent data before output mutation. Special constants propagate conservative sentinels. Post-swap special-result early return bypasses temporary teardown; source-only lifecycle observation, not an executed defect or a Hyper finite-real algorithm transfer.

Complete supporting read: Current generic dispatcher adds proved-sparse a*x^n+c composition via Taylor shift, coefficient powers and inflation. Exact finite/precision contexts use a squaring-oriented power schedule; others use sequential powers. Non-sparse outer length<=7 uses Horner, larger uses divide-and-conquer. All arithmetic statuses accumulate. Wrapper source shrink is shared implementation, not demonstrated total binary reduction.

Complete supporting read: Generic counterpart of fused first steps and parity-selected double buffering, now with context-dispatched scalar multiplication and accumulated error status. Whole-owner aliases use temporary polynomials. No arbitrary raw overlap contract inferred.

Complete supporting read: Bottom-up paired blocks and squared inner powers in one initialized vector, with separate pointer/length metadata and aggregated arithmetic status. Exact zero tests prune only proved zeros; reused workspace prevents separate allocation at each recursion level. Same sizing assumptions as the archived algorithm.

Complete supporting read: Binary exponentiation, not binomial expansion (corrects the earlier wrapper note's wording). Strips only proved low zeros, shifts output by the exponent, clamps truncation, and alternates parity-chosen scratch/output buffers. Exact 0/1/2 and constant shortcuts; generic operations accumulate statuses. Existing dense series controls exercised the public Calcium wrapper, not every generic context.

Complete supporting read: Generic strategy chooses Horner through length20, divide-and-conquer above; owner wrapper copies as needed and normalizes even after inability because generic backends may have changed or exactified leading data. Complete supporting read: In-place triangular shift uses addition/subtraction for shifts +1/-1, does nothing for proved zero and otherwise calls addmul. Hoists generic method lookup out of inner loops. Does not allocate binomial coefficients or force approximate comparisons.

Complete supporting read: Handles constant/zero-shift/linear cases then composes with [c,1] using the independently read generic divide-and-conquer kernel. Comment records a faster integer-specific algorithm elsewhere, not newly audited here.
